content.value_statement: Go code can pass formatting checks while still being hard to read. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward clearer style choices.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Go code for line length, semantic line breaks, and readable call formatting.
Guides variable declarations, empty slice initialization, and map initialization choices.
Recommends early returns, simpler control flow, and fewer unnecessary else blocks.
Advises when to use options structs instead of long parameter lists.
Explains value versus pointer parameters for common Go types and structs.
Supports large style reviews by splitting concerns across independent review passes.
limitations: It does not configure linters or replace gofmt, gofumpt, or goimports.
It does not cover identifier naming, doc comments, or interface design in depth.
It cannot prove performance claims without benchmarks from the target project.
It may need project-specific conventions to resolve style tradeoffs.

use_cases.title: Review a Go Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find readability issues in control flow, declarations, function shape, and file organization before merging.

use_cases.title: Set Team Style Standards
use_cases.description: Create a practical checklist for style decisions that are harder for automated linters to enforce.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Edits
use_cases.description: Keep generated Go code readable when prompts ask for compact code, nested branches, or excessive parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Go file for readable style. Focus on line length, variable declarations, early returns, and initialized empty collections.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor One Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Go function for clarity. Preserve behavior, reduce nesting, remove unnecessary else blocks, and explain the style changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Project Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise Go code style checklist for this repository. Align it with existing patterns and note rules linters cannot enforce.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go codebase using separate style concerns. Report findings for control flow, function design, collection initialization, and file organization.

output_examples.input: A Go handler has nested validation and returns nil slices for empty results.
output: Use early returns so validation failures exit before the happy path.
Return initialized empty slices for success cases with no results.
Keep the main response-building logic at shallow indentation.

output_examples.input: A service function accepts many separate configuration parameters.
output_examples.output: Suggest grouping related inputs into an options struct, with context first and the primary dependency near the front.

output_examples.input: A review asks whether a pointer parameter is needed for a string.
output_examples.output: Recommend passing the string by value unless nil has meaning or the function must mutate a referenced value.

best_practices: Pair this skill with gofmt, gofumpt, and goimports for mechanical formatting.
Ask for behavior-preserving edits before style refactors.
Use repository conventions when they conflict with generic style guidance.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to replace tests, linters, or compiler checks.
Applying every guideline mechanically without considering readability.
Requesting naming or documentation rules that belong to linked skills.

faq.question: Does this skill format Go code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives style guidance. Use gofmt, gofumpt, and goimports for formatting.

faq.question: Can it review existing Go code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review files or pull requests for readability and style issues.

faq.question: Does it replace a linter?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on judgment-based style choices that linters may not catch.

faq.question: Does it cover naming rules?
faq.answer: Only lightly. Naming guidance is handled by a separate Go naming skill.

faq.question: Can it help with large repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests splitting review work by independent style concerns.

faq.question: Is it specific to Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
